spike: SPIKE 4 — WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport stateless mode (sessionIdGenerator: undefined) behind Hono
claim: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js` honours `sessionIdGenerator: undefined`: `initialize` mints no `Mcp-Session-Id` header, and a later `tools/call` / `tools/list` POST with no session header succeeds — so MCPRouter can run a fully stateless downstream behind one Hono POST route.
verdict: CONFIRMED — with two mandatory implementation constraints the spec does not currently state (one transport+Server per REQUEST, and the gateway must answer GET itself).

fallback_verified: Not needed — the web-standard transport passed, so the node `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` + node-adapter shim was not run. The stateless bet holds on the web-standard path.
impact:
The bet survives, but §14 must add three implementation rules or the first tools/call in production 500s:

1. **Per-request construction, not per-process.** Stateless transports throw `Stateless transport cannot be reused across requests` on their second `handleRequest` (js:174). The spec must say: build a new `Server` AND a new transport inside the handler on every request, and `await server.connect(transport)` there. Note the SDK's own Hono example in the d.ts (`app.all('/mcp', c => transport.handleRequest(c.req.raw))` over a module-scope transport) is the wrong shape and will throw on request 2. Cost of the per-request build was invisible in the spike; if `buildServer()` gets expensive (schema compilation), memoize the handler table, not the Server.

2. **Route POST only; the gateway answers GET/DELETE/OPTIONS itself.** `app.all('/mcp', …)` into the transport is a resource leak: a stateless GET returns `200 text/event-stream` and hangs forever (js:220-250 — validateSession is a no-op, so nothing rejects it). Use `app.post('/mcp', …)` for the transport and a sibling `app.all('/mcp', …)` returning 405 `Allow: POST`. The SDK client handles that 405 correctly (verified: `client transport errors: none`).

3. **`enableJsonResponse: true` is the default for MCPRouter, not false.** It is the only mode where the transport can be closed after `handleRequest` returns — verified 0 un-closed pairs. With `false`, closing after the call kills the live stream (`MCP error -32001: Request timed out`), and not closing leaves the transport permanently un-closed with `onclose` never firing (4 leaked in the test). Flip to `false` only if/when a downstream needs progress notifications or server→client sampling mid-call, and pair that with a stream-completion cleanup hook the transport does not currently expose.

No change needed to the core claim: initialize emits no `Mcp-Session-Id`, sessionless follow-up POSTs succeed, and the real SDK Client is happy with `sessionId === undefined`.
gotchas: js:174 — a stateless transport handles exactly ONE request, then throws `Stateless transport cannot be reused across requests. Create a new transport per request.` Verified live: POST#2 to a shared transport returned 500. This is the single biggest trap, and the SDK's own Hono snippet in the .d.ts (lines 142-145) demonstrates the broken shape.

GET on a stateless transport returns 200 text/event-stream and hangs open indefinitely — it does NOT 405. `validateSession` returns undefined immediately when sessionIdGenerator is undefined (js:726), so nothing rejects the stream. The built-in 405 (`Allow: GET, POST, DELETE`) only fires for methods outside GET/POST/DELETE — PUT and OPTIONS got 405, GET did not.

enableJsonResponse:false is NOT drop-in behind a Hono handler that cleans up: `handleRequest` resolves with a live ReadableStream, so `await transport.close()` right after truncates it and the client fails with `MCP error -32001: Request timed out`. With true, the Response is fully buffered (content-length: 143) and close-after is safe.

Never closing an SSE-mode stateless transport does not fire `onclose` and leaves the Server attached — 4 un-closed transports after one client session. No timer/socket handles leaked (keep-alive intervals are cleared by the stream cleanup), so it is a GC-pressure leak, not a handle leak — but there is no completion hook to close them on.

`Accept: application/json` alone gets 406 even when enableJsonResponse is true — the transport demands BOTH `application/json` and `text/event-stream` in Accept (js:~533). Any non-SDK client MCPRouter proxies for must send both.
DELETE on a stateless transport returns 200 with an empty body (no Allow header). If MCPRouter wants DELETE to mean anything, it must own that route too.

A stale/bogus `Mcp-Session-Id` header on an inbound request is silently ignored in stateless mode (200), so a client that cached a session id from some other gateway will not break — and MCPRouter gets no signal that it happened.

`MCP-Protocol-Version` is optional on non-initialize POSTs (absent -> 200), but a bogus value is a hard 400 from the transport before your code sees it. Supported list as of 1.30.0: 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05, 2024-10-07.

`@hono/node-server@2.1.1` is present only as a TRANSITIVE dep of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (`npm ls` shows it nested under the SDK). It worked (`serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: 0, hostname })`, then `srv.address().port`), but MCPRouter must declare it as a direct dependency rather than rely on hoisting.
The transport takes `c.req.raw` (the Web Request), not `c.req` (Hono's wrapper). Passing `c.req` fails.
